definition: The official product name. The only permitted expansion of TOS.
The official short name for TopShelf Operating System.
Stable schemas, state model, policy evaluation, contract system, and validation primitives.
Executable services and CLI that inspect, schedule, constrain, verify, promote, recover, and upgrade projects.
Versioned package of contracts, controls, workflows, and checks activated by project facts.
Provider-specific implementation of an agnostic TOS capability.
A repository or initiative governed by a specific TOS version and project manifest.
A versioned, owned, testable statement of obligations, permissions, prohibitions, failure behavior, and evidence.
The complete list of named foundation concerns that every project must evaluate.
Evidence-backed record of current and intended project state.
TOS subsystem that inspects evidence, compares declarations, classifies facts, detects conflict, and asks targeted questions.
Machine-readable dependency graph of work, decisions, blockers, and gates.
A bounded end-to-end unit of value or control that can be independently implemented and proven.
Compiled execution contract for a human or AI function.
Time-bounded claim on a task and resource scope.
Version-bound proof supporting a specific claim and evidence class.
Controlled transition from one lifecycle state to another.
Deliberate invalid condition proving that a checker or gate can fail correctly.
The human with final business authority: Patrick Craven unless formally delegated.
An accountable operating responsibility; it may be performed by Patrick, an AI agent, or another authorized person.
Authoritative human-readable records under `.tos/`.
Rebuildable indexes, caches, summaries, or views that are not authoritative.
Deny or block when authority, scope, state, evidence, or applicability cannot be determined safely.
An explicit evaluated disposition with recorded reason and authority; never an omitted contract.
